text: The provider is policy-backed today and does not claim semantic decision capability.
IPC v3 is a distinct protocol and does not negotiate down to IPC v2.
Private signing material belongs to the provider process, not the HTTP server.
The network namespace is absent from the terminal execution capability.
A context digest identifies supplied evidence but does not prove human approval.
The manifest records corpus version, creation date, file names, and sample counts.
Corpus releases are immutable; new samples belong in a new version directory.
The deployment guide keeps the API bound to loopback until remote authentication exists.
Systemd credentials are delivered through a file descriptor instead of environment variables.
The threat model treats planner-provided context as untrusted evidence.
A semantic assessment reports the model and reference corpus digests it used.
Missing required semantic evidence must not be replaced by a default score.
The public key bundle is integrity-sensitive even though its contents are public.
The audit ledger hashes redacted event details before durable storage.
A timeout is a failed decision dependency and therefore fails closed.
Human approval is bound to the exact normalized proposal being executed.
The Rust Book introduces ownership as a compile-time memory-management discipline.
Rust editions organize language changes while allowing crates from different editions to interoperate.
A trait describes behavior that types can implement and generic code can require.
Lifetimes describe how long references remain valid; they do not extend the referenced value.
Option represents a value that may be absent without using a null pointer convention.
The standard library provides filesystem, collections, synchronization, and I/O APIs.
Mutex provides mutual exclusion for access to data shared between threads.
Path represents filesystem paths using platform-aware path components.
Command configures a child process and can collect its exit status and output.
